newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds dip but outperform neighbours.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds dip but outperform neighbours.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds slipped on Friday in featureless trading on a combination of worries of a U.S. rate rise, higher than expected U.S. industrial production data and the long weekend there, but still outperformed Bunds.
Traders said it was hard to predict where prices would go next, but that domestic buyers still had plenty of cash to spare even if the market appeared too expensive for most foreign players.
"The market was a bit weaker today but still outperformed its neighbours, particularly Germany," one trader said, adding that few end-investors were in the market on Friday.
"There was less interest in the longer end than in previous days," one trader said. "There was more focus on the medium, five to 10-year, maturities."

Traders said the market had spent the day in the red due to comments overnight from a member of the U.S. Federal Reserve, warning of a possible tightening of interest rates if jobless figures kept falling.

This, coupled with the industrial production data for December that came in slightly above forecast and the Martin Luther King Day holiday on Monday in the United States, combined to pressure prices slightly.

"The spread (over Germany) is still too narrow, but the market will stay up," one trader said. "If I was a foreign buyer I would not step into this market because it is too expensive. It is domestic buyers who are pushing it up."
The yield of the benchmark 2007 OLO ended the day at 5.81 percent, up from Thursday's closing 5.78. The spread over Bunds eased to six basis points from seven.
The March futures contract was 12 basis points down at 121.65, having moved in a narrow 121.73/121.53 range.
